text:
alex: quick heads-up — hitting a routing mismatch for private VPC customers. dedicated pool routing seems to ignore X-Workspace-ID when request originates from a mapped VPC endpoint. Repro below.

alex: repro:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $$$" \
     -H "X-Workspace-ID: wks_abc123" \
     https://private.redwood.example/edge/v1/generate
```
ingress-bot: route chosen: private-endpoint -> vpc-mapped -> pool: default-shared
alex: expected: route -> dedicated-pool for wks_abc123 (customer has dedicated capacity)
sophie: :eyes: is the workspace id being ignored or overridden by VPC mapping? logs?
alex: snippet from router logs:
```
2026-02-14T15:02:11Z | src_ip=10.2.3.4 | vpc_id=vpc-998 | x-workspace-id=wks_abc123 | matched_rule=vpc_mapping:vpc-998 -> tenant_scope=UNSET
```
samir: ah — router sets tenant_scope=UNSET when vpc mapping exists. that's our old behavior (vpc mappings win). it's intentional for security (VPC => network-level tenancy). but this causes problems when customers have both VPC mapping and want to access dedicated pools by header.
lia: customers with private endpoints usually expect network trust to determine tenant, not header spoofing. header overrides are risky.
alex: but in this case customer actually has dedicated pool bound to workspace and we need to route to that pool. header shouldn't be ignored if we can verify workspace ownership via auth token / mTLS.
sophie: suggestion: change precedence: if Authorization token maps to same workspace as X-Workspace-ID, honor header and route to dedicated pool. otherwise, continue to use vpc mapping and log a metric.
jordan: proposed matching order:
1) authenticate token -> determine workspace (auth_workspace)
2) if auth_workspace == X-Workspace-ID -> use workspace-scoped routing (check dedicated pools)
3) else if vpc mapping exists -> use vpc mapping (network trust)
4) otherwise -> default shared pool
samir: +1 but need to guard against header missing; also guard if token absent but mTLS present (client cert binds workspace) — treat that as auth_workspace.
alex: agree. also add telemetry: metric `routing.override_header_verified` with labels {workspace, vpc, route_outcome}
sophie: can we implement a fast-path in the ingress proxy (envoy filter) to short-circuit? don't want to add heavy auth lookup on every request if token present.
samir: we already cache token->workspace in redis for 60s; cost should be minimal. main change is logic order in router service.
lia: security sign-off: we'll need threat model note — header should not be trusted alone. require token or mTLS. update docs for customers: "If you use VPC mapping and want to target dedicated pools using X-Workspace-ID, include an auth token or mTLS that proves ownership."
alex: dev plan:
- infra: add auth_workspace resolution before vpc mapping (samir)
- router: implement precedence rule + metric (sophie)
- ingress: add small envoy filter to pull auth header into route metadata (jordan)
- security: create short threat doc and approve (lia)
- docs: update routing page and examples (samir/jordan)
alex: ETA? can we target next deploy window (Thu deploy)?
sophie: I can pick up router change, will need ~1 day + tests.
samir: infra change is small, will be ready tomorrow.
lia: security review 1 day.
jordan: I'll do the envoy change but need to sync with deploy schedule.
alex: ok assign: sophie (router PR), jordan (envoy), samir (cache + infra), lia (security sign-off), alex (docs + rollout)
ingress-bot: ticket created: PLAT-3427 — "Respect verified X-Workspace-ID for VPC-mapped requests"
alex: adding acceptance criteria:
- requests with valid token/mTLS and X-Workspace-ID route to the workspace's dedicated pool if exists
- all others follow existing vpc mapping behavior
- metric `routing.override_header_verified` emitted with value 1 on success
sophie: will add unit + integration tests + a harness scenario simulating both vpc and header.
samir: also adding a patch to telemetry to tag traces with routing_origin:{header_verified|vpc|default}
alex: cool. we'll do canary and monitor latency/cost. post-merge steps: update Console docs + telemetry dashboard.
jordan: FYI — a previous similar change caused a spike in cache misses; keep an eye on token cache hit rate.
lia: noted.
alex: thanks all. I'll drop notes in eng-qa and customer-ops.
sophie: :thumbsup: 
samir: :rocket: 
alex: end.
